body.statement: Assume that \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\) is nonempty for all sufficiently large \(T\), equivalently that the bounded-support variance floor is feasible: \(\kappa\leq1\) if \(\alpha>0\), and \(\kappa\leq2\) if \(\alpha=0\). On \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), the ordinary interval \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\), computed from outcomes observed through \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\), is uniformly asymptotically honest if and only if \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\). If this product converges to a positive finite constant, a compatible hidden-sign family has a nonzero shifted-Gaussian limit and ordinary-Wald undercoverage; if it diverges, ordinary-Wald coverage tends to zero along a compatible family. At \(\Delta_T=0\), ordinary Wald is uniformly honest exactly when \(\beta>q\).
body.justification: Because follow-up changes both truncation ages and the observations entering the statistic, the uniform if-and-only-if criterion separates a class-wide ordinary-Wald guarantee, a class-wide tail-padding requirement, and sufficient endpoint follow-up.
body.gap: Classical delayed urn inference gives usual asymptotics, and delayed CARA theory assumes ignorable delays; neither characterizes the informative-tail follow-up boundary.
body.consumer: A protocol can select no pad, a bias-aware pad, or additional follow-up from the prespecified exploration and endpoint-tail exponents.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(|Y(a)|\leq1\), \(\operatorname{Var}_P\{Y(a)\}\leq1\).  Thus nonemptiness of \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\) requires \(\kappa\leq1\) if \(\alpha>0\), and \(\kappa\leq2\) if \(\alpha=0\).  Conversely, under the respective restriction, take prompt symmetric Rademacher outcomes in both arms, zero delays, and \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\).  Then \(\pi_t(0)\geq1-c\geq\varepsilon\), so this law belongs to the regular class and proves sufficiency of the feasibility restriction.

On the regular class, the variance comparison
\[
 |\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq g_{T,\Delta}\})
   -\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(a))|
 \leq3P\{D(a)>g_{T,\Delta}\}=o(1)                                      \tag{1}
\]
and the quota orders imply constants \(0<c_0<C_0<\infty\) such that
\[
 c_0T^{-(1-\alpha)}\leq s_{T,\Delta}^2
 \leq C_0T^{-(1-\alpha)}.                                                \tag{2}
\]
For the lower bound, arm one suffices when \(\alpha>0\); when \(\alpha=0\), both quotas are comparable to \(T\).  The upper bound uses \(\sigma_{a,T}^2\leq1\).  The uniform studentized theorem gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau}{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}
 =\frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}}
        {\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}
  -\frac{b_{T,\Delta}}{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}},                          \tag{3}
\]
where the first term converges uniformly to \(N(0,1)\), and \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1\).  The bias bound and (2) imply
\[
 \sup_{\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)}
 \frac{|b_{T,\Delta}|}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 \leq C_1T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}.                       \tag{4}
\]
If the right side tends to zero, the second term in (3) is uniformly \(o_P(1)\).  Hence the ordinary interval with critical value \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) is uniformly asymptotically honest.

For necessity, set
\[
 \delta_T=\min\{1/4,L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\},                                \tag{5}
\]
use \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\), and index a triangular family by \(\gamma\in\{-1,1\}\).  Put \(s_1=\gamma\), \(s_0=-\gamma\).  Independently over arrivals and arms, with probability \(\delta_T\) set
\[
 (D_t(a),Y_t(a))=(H_T+1,s_a),                                            \tag{6}
\]
and with probability \(1-\delta_T\) set \(D_t(a)=0\) and draw \(Y_t(a)\in\{-1,1\}\) with mean
\[
 -\frac{\delta_Ts_a}{1-\delta_T}.                                      \tag{7}
\]
The mean in (7) is admissible because \(\delta_T\leq1/4\).  For every integer \(u\geq0\),
\[
 P\{D_t(a)>u\}=
 \begin{cases}
  \delta_T,&0\leq u\leq H_T,\\
  0,&u\geq H_T+1,
 \end{cases}
 \leq\min\{1,L(1+u)^{-\beta}\}.                                      \tag{8}
\]
All outcomes are bounded and all delays are finite.  Direct calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PY_t(a)=0,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_P\{Y_t(a)\}=1,                              \tag{9}
\]
so the construction belongs to every support-feasible regular class.  Because \(g_{T,\Delta}<h_{T,\Delta}<H_T+1\), its correction variables vanish and
\[
 b_{T,\Delta}=2\gamma\delta_T.                                          \tag{10}
\]
The visible variables have variance \(1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2\to1\).  Integral comparison gives
\[
 \frac{T^{1-\alpha}}{K_1(n_T)}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\alpha}{c},
 \qquad
 \frac{T}{K_0(n_T)}\longrightarrow\frac1\varepsilon\quad(\alpha=0).  \tag{11}
\]
Consequently, for some fixed \(s_*>0\),
\[
 T^{(1-\alpha)/2}s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow s_*.                       \tag{12}
\]
Since the second term in (5) is eventually active, (10)--(12) imply
\[
 \frac{b_{T,\Delta}}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 =\frac{2\gamma L}{s_*}
 T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}.                            \tag{13}
\]
If the product in (13) converges to a finite positive constant, choose \(\gamma=1\).  Equation (3) then converges to \(N(-u,1)\) for some \(u>0\), and ordinary-Wald coverage converges to
\[
 \Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}-u)+\Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}+u)-1<1-\eta.                  \tag{14}
\]
The strict inequality follows by differentiating the left side with respect to \(u>0\).  If the product diverges, the centered term in (3) remains tight while the absolute shift diverges, so coverage tends to zero.  Because \(\delta_T\to0\), truncation by \([-2,2]\) is asymptotically irrelevant.  If the product fails to tend to zero, take a subsequence bounded away from zero and then a further subsequence on which it either converges to a positive finite limit or diverges.  Thus uniform honesty is impossible unless
\[
 T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0.              \tag{15}
\]
This proves the equivalence.  At \(\Delta_T=0\), the left side of (15) is \(T^{(1-\alpha)/2-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}\), which tends to zero exactly when \(\beta>(1-\alpha)/2=q\).
